name: Engine
summary: Atlas's always-on engine on the Raspberry Pi, formerly the separate the Engine. Its functions run there today (Engine dashboard, Telegram, command line, automatic jobs); Atlas's screen reaches them once the hub connection exists (RA-030).
repository: Djeddozo/Unconventional-Reasoning-Atlas (engine/ package, old name hq/; formerly Djeddozo/the former app)
authority: Engine owns its data (ADR-005); Atlas never writes hq.db.

domains.name: Cortex
domains.summary: Atlas's reasoning core: reason together, capture and sort thoughts, intake, voice.

domains.name: Forge
domains.summary: Ideas → Plan → Build: placing ideas, the plan, and the dev loop that builds it.

domains.name: Direction
domains.summary: Goals, plans and priorities; what to do next and why.

domains.name: Skill tree
domains.summary: Capabilities, their state and proof, and how to build the next one.

domains.name: Assets
domains.summary: What you have: resources and the arsenal of everything you built.

domains.name: Research
domains.summary: Investigating options with sources, and finding reusable software.

domains.name: Memory
domains.summary: Decisions, attempts and lessons Engine has learned.

domains.name: Owner attention
domains.summary: What only the owner can settle: needs, approvals, terminal steps, work stopped by usage limits.

domains.name: System
domains.summary: The engine keeping itself healthy: usage and kill switch, budgets, models, updates, repairs.

capabilities.summary: Write a thought to the brain; the engine sorts it into the plan.
Show recent thoughts and what the brain made of each (sorted, waiting for a model, or kept as a note).
Turn free text, typed or spoken, into structured additions to the plan.
capabilities.note: In Atlas through Talk (engine.brain.talk): statements are sorted by this function.

capabilities.summary: Sort waiting thoughts into ideas, tasks or memories, hourly or on demand.
Decide where a thought belongs: the task-versus-idea rule and the place in the plan.
Accept or dismiss what the brain suggests.
capabilities.note: In Atlas folded into the do-over: open drop/merge suggestions count as drift, and the diff waits on Today.

capabilities.summary: Undo plan changes from the change log, including the 7-second Undo after an action.
Take in a link, image or PDF and file it as memory.
Read PDFs: text first, a picture of the first page for scans.
Speak a thought and see the transcript live; edit it, then ask Cortex or file it (GPU PC, Pi or cloud Whisper, or browser speech).
capabilities.note: One voice path (task #143): in Atlas, Quick note 🎙 shows the transcript live (browser speech, or Whisper on the GPU PC, Pi or cloud), editable before it is sent to Cortex or filed; Telegram voice messages use the same Whisper tiers, set up under Systems.

capabilities.summary: Retry recordings that could not be transcribed when they arrived.

Talk to Atlas as to Claude: a question is answered from your plan (mode ask always answers), anything else is sorted into visions, objectives, goals, tasks, ideas, skill-tree nodes or memories, with what changed and where, and undo. The one chat path, the same in the app and on Telegram.
The recent conversation with Atlas (your questions and Claude's answers).
Your conversations with Cortex, newest first, to go back to an earlier one.
Coding agents as switchable resources: which are installed, which are out of usage, your fallback order, and a hand-over prompt any agent can start from.
Set the fallback order of coding agents and list the installed ones under Resources.
Idea cards with where each fits in the plan, plus saved research.
Suggest for every open idea an existing path or a new one, with a reason.
Explore an idea: which visions and goals it serves and how, why it is worth having, how it could start something new, a first step, risks, and whether to take it as a task, a goal or later.
Take an idea into the plan: the AI decides task or goal from its exploration (or the placement), or you choose the goal yourself.
Before building: does this already exist in the engine, the arsenal or the backlog?
capabilities.note: In Atlas: the task detail ("Already in Atlas?") and holds on Today.

capabilities.summary: What has to be there first for a task or node; informs, never blocks.
capabilities.note: One home for what must exist first, for a task or a skill-tree node (merged from engine.growth.prerequisites, #128). In Atlas: the task detail, the skill tree ("Needs first") and Research ("Before you start").

capabilities.summary: The plan as one tree: mission, nested goals by horizon, tasks.
Create and edit tasks, ideas, goals and skill-tree nodes; nest goals.
Mark tasks doing, to do, done, dropped or deleted; set the owner.
Move a task up or down, or back to automatic ranking.
Every task and idea in one list with filters and what blocks what.
Readable evidence behind a task, with model reasoning kept apart from facts.
Claude re-evaluates the whole open plan (keep, change, done, drop, merge, new), automatically after real change and daily, or on request; applied only after approval, undoable.
capabilities.note: One home for re-evaluating the plan (merged from engine.brain.reevaluate_plan, #124): the brain's re-prioritisation runs first, then a do-over is drafted when the plan drifted. Also hq brain think, hq doover replan and Telegram /think.

capabilities.summary: A plan re-evaluation in short: what changes mainly and why, the counts, and the changed tasks with their reasons.
Turn an idea into a build proposal for the dev loop, shown before submission.
capabilities.note: In Atlas: Forge › Build (engine.build.quick_build).

capabilities.summary: An explicit build request goes straight to the dev loop.
Claude Code on the Pi builds AI tasks one per run on a branch and opens a pull request.
capabilities.note: Runs only when enabled on the Pi (deploy/enable-devloop.sh) and within your limits.

capabilities.summary: Pause, resume, stop, autonomy level, batch size and daily limits of the dev loop.
Live lanes and step-by-step console for every task in flight: each step one plain sentence (engine/buildsteps.py, #179), raw output behind Output.
Your queue first, then the engine's proposals; queue drafts or move to the top.
Approve or refuse big or outside-code builds before they start.
capabilities.note: In Atlas through Today › Waiting on you (engine.attention.answer_needs).

capabilities.summary: Save a task's progress before a usage, turn, time or context limit.
Pick a light, standard or strong model per task, with the reason logged.
capabilities.note: In Atlas: the model and its reason show on each run in Forge › Build.

capabilities.summary: Scan open pull requests for conflicts with main and resolve them.
Pull requests from draft to merged to installed; tasks close only on evidence.
capabilities.note: In Atlas: Forge › Build and the update panel (engine.build.run_status).

capabilities.summary: Reconnect the Claude subscription on the Pi through the official command-line tool.
Each build works on its own snapshot of the database, never on live memory.
Current focus, next step and destination.
Lifetime visions with their year objectives on a timeline, progress and momentum, and a recommended focus that explains itself.
Choose the vision to focus on; the ranking gives its work a bonus, so the Forge follows.
Create visions and year objectives, and place goals under a vision (undoable).
Choose the build mode: plan first, balanced, ideas first or management agent first.
One ranked list of what to do next, re-ranked when something changes.
Why a task ranks where it does, and the full build explanation (problem, why now, expected result, goal, dependencies, effort, uncertainty, success criterion; missing reasoning shown as missing).
The queue rolled up into skill-tree nodes and goals: what it all builds towards.
capabilities.note: Data built; its view awaits your design choice (docs/design/ZOOM_OUT.md).

capabilities.summary: The daily brief: what changed, what is next, what needs you.
capabilities.note: In Atlas: Today at a glance (engine.direction.progress and next steps).

capabilities.summary: The engine's loop: observe, re-evaluate, re-rank, log, brief.
Streaks, completed work and how the plan is moving.
Write the week's review: what was done, goals, what slipped, focus for next week, with a short observation by Claude when reachable; saved to memory.
Capabilities with state (unlocked, building, available, locked) and build order.
Outside code tested in a Docker sandbox without network or credentials: result, scan flags and output, plus the security gate (source, trust, licence), as evidence for the manual approval.
capabilities.note: Runs start from the CLI (hq sandbox run / check); a screen section is a follow-up.

capabilities.summary: How sure the engine is that a skill is held: confirmed, partly shown, suggested or not yet.
Confirm or dismiss suggested proof for a skill.
Research how to build a node: outside tools, your arsenal or build it; pick one to draft a task.
Link open tasks to the skill-tree node they build, with undo.
Draft the task that builds a node, for you to queue.
Search everything you have built, for reuse.
Index your project folders again into the arsenal; adding a new folder stays on the command line.
Your resources: money, hardware, accounts, time, skills, contacts, services.
Add, correct or retire a resource; undoable, nothing is deleted, never secrets.
Drag the builder's queue into your own order; what you place there is built first, in that order.
A machine (the Pi itself, or Atlas on the PC through the hub) reports its CPU, memory, GPUs and disk as one live resource.
Scan GitHub, Hacker News, arXiv, Hugging Face, lab blogs and followed releases, ranked against your interests.
capabilities.note: Runs by itself every few hours; Scan now under Research › Sources & limits.

capabilities.summary: Developments and tools that touch Atlas or your interests, with why they matter and what a tool needs first.
Save a finding for later, hide it, or bring it back.
Review which interests produced useful hits and which noise after the first scans; mute, boost or add interests used for ranking.
Choose feeds and per-source limits.
Deep research: one question answered for what you build, with sources.
capabilities.note: One model call; can cost time and money.

capabilities.summary: Read the sourced answer of a finished investigation.
Turn a research item or answer into a named idea.
Watch for GitHub tools and skills to try in a sandbox.
capabilities.note: Phase 3 in Engine's roadmap.

capabilities.summary: Recall decisions, lessons, preferences and facts relevant to a topic.
Browse the Engine's memory by kind and words: lessons, decisions, preferences, facts, research notices.
Record a lesson, decision, preference or fact; Cortex also files them from your thoughts.
Claude reads the engine's memory and proposes what should change.
capabilities.note: Built, switched off until Phase 2.

capabilities.summary: Every change with who made it and why; the basis for undo.
What only you can settle: decisions, approvals and your own tasks an agent waits for; answer in place.
Answer a need by tap, typing or voice.
Approve or deny requests: spending, access, sending, publishing, installing.
capabilities.note: In Atlas through Today › Waiting on you (engine.attention.answer_needs).

capabilities.summary: Decide routine agent actions automatically; ask you only for decisions.
Steps an agent left for you to run, with the command and the reason.
Mark a terminal step as done or no longer needed.
Work Claude Code, Codex or the dev loop could not finish because of a usage limit, with a resume prompt.
Mark work stopped by a usage limit as finished or not needed.
'Already done?' suggestions when merged work mentions a task.
capabilities.note: In Atlas through Today › Waiting on you (engine.attention.answer_needs).

capabilities.summary: Token use, cost and budgets per job.
Systems at a glance: kill switch, budgets per job, model routing, automatic repairs, the self-maintenance jobs with their last run, voice and Claude sign-in, and the constitution (read-only).
Test each way of transcribing voice (GPU PC, Pi, cloud) and set the GPU PC's address; keys stay in the Pi's .env.
Stop all agent work at once, and resume.
Daily limits on paid model use per background job; falls back to rules or local models.
Send each job to the cheapest model that does it well: GPU PC, Pi or cloud.
Install merged work from GitHub after its tests pass on the Pi, then restart.
Which version the Pi runs, how many changes wait on GitHub, and how the last update went.
Watchdog: deduplicate crashes, build fixes, test and install small repairs. Switched on or off under Systems.

Monthly review of features built earlier (keep, improve, merge, remove) and of where every function lives (move, merge, remove); proposals become draft tasks. Also after every change to the structure.
Weekly recheck of the outside tools and models the engine uses.
The engine's timed jobs on the Pi.
Brief, approvals, thoughts and questions from your phone.
The engine's own dashboard over Tailscale with an access token.
Export the plan (goals, tasks, skill-tree nodes, ideas, resources, runs, research) as one read-only snapshot for Atlas's read model.
capabilities.note: RA-009: works on an in-memory copy (no rescore, no planning cycle); missing columns answer 409 schema_mismatch. Evidence STATE/evidence/RA-009.md.

capabilities.summary: Daily encrypted snapshot of the owner's data to a separate private repository; the public repository never holds data. Shown under Systems › Self-maintenance.
The name of Atlas's reasoning core: Cortex, or the nickname the owner gave it.
Give Cortex a nickname (shown everywhere in Atlas; the reasoning core answers to it).
Speak to Cortex from any screen: it reads what is shown and proposes up to three numbered actions; nothing runs until the owner says yes.
One turn of the Cortex chat on Claude Code: streamed answer, real conversation turns, web search, Atlas look-ups, attached files; changes only as numbered proposals.
Attach a file to the current Cortex conversation so Cortex can read it.
The Build next lane: put a task at a place (1 = next), reorder or take it out; the builder takes these first, before the queue and any score. Undoable.
Ready AI tasks with no blockers between them and no files in common, proposed as one batch to build side by side, with why the others are left out.
Accept the proposed batch of independent tasks (only these may fill the builder's extra slots) or dismiss that set. Undoable.
Start a new conversation with Cortex, or go back to an earlier one; nothing is deleted.
Visual first: tasks with a visual side waiting for the choice 'mockup first or build without', and every mockup with its rounds.
Start a mockup of a UI feature, add rounds made in Claude or ChatGPT (picture or HTML), and hold the build until the owner approves it.
How long newly added tasks, ideas and goals stand out as new (Today's Just added, the plan list and the goal tree).
Apply an option Cortex offered (one action or a bundle of steps, all or nothing, one Undo); the other options stay open.
What Cortex may do at once: routine plan changes with Undo (default), or offer every change first.

adapter: Read-only snapshot adapter (RA-008) connected through the hub's snapshot export (RA-009): engine/export.py → engine.system.snapshot_export → services/atlas/enginesync.py. Writes stay disabled (RA-010).
